diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, if all eigenvalues of $P(\lambda)$ are simple, i.e, $n_j=1$ for all $j=1,\ldots r$.

issues.failure_explanation: For |λ|=1 the partner 1/λ̄ equals λ itself, so a unimodular eigenvalue is self-paired. Its Jordan structure need not consist of two identical copies, and its algebraic multiplicity need not be even. Counterexample: n=1, P(λ)=λ²+qλ+1 with real |q|<2 is H-palindromic. It has two distinct simple unimodular eigenvalues e^{±iθ}, which Case 2 cannot represent: each unimodular group would have size 2n_j≥2, giving total size ≥4>2n. Consequently Corollary cor-1, which is stated for simple eigenvalues (n_j=1), assigns a 2×2 block Ψ_j to what is actually a double eigenvalue diag(λ_j,λ_j). Theorem thm-s-2 instead uses blocks E_j of order n_j, which is inconsistent with the 2n_j-sized Case-2 blocks.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unimodular Case-2 blocks by single blocks λ_jI+N_j and restate the corresponding Γ_jj as a single block in Θ_(λ_j, λ̄_j, j) with Γ_jj^H=-εΓ_jj. Then correct the block sizes in thm-gamma-2, cor-1 (scalars in iR or R for simple unimodular eigenvalues) and thm-s-2. The same Sylvester-equation arguments apply.
issues.overall_effect: The structure results for the H-palindromic and H-anti-palindromic cases (thm-gamma-2, cor-1 H-part, thm-s-2) apply only to a non-generic subclass. Generic polynomials with simple or non-paired unimodular eigenvalues are excluded, contrary to the claimed characterization of Γ.

issues.why_classification: The proofs carry over, but the setup and the statements of three results must be rewritten to restore the advertised scope; this is more than a local fix, yet it needs no new architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Entrywise, the defining equation reads aZ_{s,t+1}+bZ_{s+1,t}+Z_{s+1,t+1}=0. For blocks of sizes 3 and 2 this gives Z_{12}(2,2)=Z_{12}(3,1)=Z_{12}(3,2)=0 and aZ_{12}(1,2)+bZ_{12}(2,1)=0. The entries (1,2) and (2,1) can therefore be nonzero, as Example exa1 itself shows with f_{12} and f_{21}. The stated rule s+t≥max{3,2}=3 would wrongly force them to zero. The correct threshold is s+t≥min{n_i,n_k}+2, which also agrees with the diagonal-block rule.

issues.failure_explanation: The T-palindromic forms in cor-1 are given for the real representation J_R, but thm-IEP pairs them with a complex diagonal Λ. For a quadruple ordered as (λ, λ̄, 1/λ, 1/λ̄), the condition ΛΓΛ^T=Γ forces the (1,4) entry b to vanish, since λ/λ̄≠1. Hence cor-1 blocks with b≠0 are not in S_(Λ,T,1), and the sufficiency part of main-thm does not apply. If the constructed A,Q solved the problem, the canonical Γ would equal this Γ and lie in S_Λ, a contradiction.
